questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the literal meaning of tuōlājī?
What three parts of speech can píngjūn be?
What is -tái the counter for, and what does it literally mean?
Is a verb necessary in měige dàduì èrshitái?
What does the pattern hái...duō... express?
Write the Chinese for "The average salary of Chinese workers is not much."

answers.answer_text: Zhōngguó gōngrénde píngjūn shōurù bù duō.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "When you average it out, each of us has ten dollars."

answers.answer_text: Píngjūnqǐlai wǒmen měige rén yǒu shíkuài qián.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "I would like to study Chinese for another few months."

answers.answer_text: Wǒ hái xīwàng duō xué jǐge yuè Zhōngwén.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Is tuōlājī purely a sound borrowing?

answers.answer_text: Not purely — it may be a sound borrowing from "tractor," but it also makes good sense in Chinese as "drag-pull-machine."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "one teacher for every five students on the average."

articles.text:
11. A: Nǐmen gōngshè yǒu zhème duō   Your commune has so many large tractors!
       dà tuōlājī!
    B: Ng, píngjūn měige dàduì      Yes, every brigade has twenty on the
       èrshitái, wǒmen hái xiǎng     average, and we want to buy a few more!
       duō mǎi jǐtái ne!

Notes on No. 11

tuōlājī: "tractor." This word MAY be a sound borrowing from the English word "tractor," but it ALSO MAKES GOOD SENSE in Chinese, since the parts mean literally "DRAG-PULL-MACHINE."

píngjūn: "average." This can be used as an ADJECTIVE, an ADVERB, or a VERB:

Zhōngguó gōngrénde píngjūn       The average salary of Chinese workers is
shōurù bù duō.                   not much.
Píngjūnqǐlai wǒmen měige rén     When you average it out, each of us has
yǒu shíkuài qián.                ten dollars.

-tái: Literally "PLATFORM" (as in zhàntái, "station platform"), this is the COUNTER FOR MACHINES.

měige dàduì èrshitái: "twenty for each brigade." NO VERB IS NECESSARY here. Compare:

Yíge rén yíkuài.                 One piece per person.
měige xīngqī yícì                once every week
Wǒmen xuéxiào píngjūn wǔge       In our school, there is one teacher for
xuésheng yíge lǎoshī.            every five students on the average.

hái xiǎng duō mǎi jǐtái: "still want to buy a few more." English "more" sometimes CONTAINS the meaning of "still, additionally" (hái), so "still" is not absolutely necessary in the English translation. Look at other examples of the common pattern HÁI...DUŌ...:

Zhèige xiǎo nánháizi hái xiǎng   This little boy wanted to eat another
duō chī yíge píngguǒ.            apple.
Wǒ hái xīwàng duō xué jǐge yuè   I would like to study Chinese for another
Zhōngwén.                        few months.
Tā hái děi duō děng jǐtiān cái   He still has to wait another few days
néng zǒu.                        before he can leave.
